data.name: Ghasaan
data.gender_notes: Ghasaan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'ghasas' meaning 'to be firm, to stand strong'. In Islamic history, Ghasaan ibn Al-As was a legendary warrior and king who ruled over Syria and Jordan. The name Ghasaan carries the meaning “Strong, Firm” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghasaan usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, firm and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and determination in the path of righteousness.
data.etymology: Ghasaan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, Firm.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghasaan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_urdu.name: غسان

Historically, the name Ghasaan has been used to signify individuals known for their honesty, moral integrity, and spiritual guidance. It holds spiritual significance in Islamic tradition as a descriptor of a person with admirable character traits.
